title: Opening a network file on Windows
body: I'm a new Helix user, accustomed to nvim on Unix, using hx 23.03 on Windows 10 by double-clicking hx.exe. I can't open a file from my synced network desktop. Dragging a UNC file such as "\\1.2.3.4\UsersFiles\me\Desktop\file.txt" onto Helix leaves malformed text on the command line and does not open it. Dragging a local file also does not open it unless I first enter `:o `. A local path then opens, but entering or dragging the network path after `:o ` freezes and advances only one character about every ten seconds. I also cannot paste the copied path: Ctrl-V inserts a literal `v`, Ctrl-Shift-V inserts a literal `V`, and mouse clicks do nothing. Is there any way for me to open this file?

symptoms_visible: Dragging a UNC file onto Helix does not open it and leaves malformed path text on the command line.
After `:o `, a local path opens normally, but a UNC path freezes and advances by roughly one character every ten seconds.
Ctrl-V and Ctrl-Shift-V insert literal letters, while right and middle mouse clicks do not paste.
N0.label: N0 UNC file cannot be opened normally

symptoms_visible: The standalone hx.exe window still does not accept the system clipboard through the shortcuts I tried, and the UNC path remains too slow to enter in `:o`.
N1.label: N1 launch and clipboard environment established

symptoms_visible: After enabling Ctrl-Shift-V in the Windows console settings, I can paste into the editor, but pasting the UNC path into `:o` still takes about 13 seconds per character.
N2_x.label: N2_x console paste enabled but core issue remains

symptoms_visible: The delay occurs only when the path has the leading UNC `\\`; removing that prefix makes the otherwise similar string paste quickly.
The complete UNC string pastes into the editor pane immediately, but the same string trickles into the `:o` command prompt at about 13 seconds per character.
N3.label: N3 delay isolated to UNC input in open prompt

symptoms_visible: The same UNC-path slowdown still occurs in Windows Terminal 1.18 and in Helix 23.10.
Dragging the path after an intentionally invalid `:e ` command inserts it immediately, while dragging it after `:o ` stalls when the path reaches a directory containing many subdirectories.
N4_x.label: N4_x bracketed-paste explanation falsified

symptoms_visible: After copying the file path and entering `:o <C-r>*`, the UNC path appears in its extended `\\?\UNC\...` form and the network file opens much more efficiently.
N_terminal.label: terminal efficient clipboard-register workaround confirmed

question_patterns: How exactly are you launching Helix on Windows, and what kind of window appears?
Are you starting hx from a terminal, or double-clicking hx.exe directly?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm double-clicking hx.exe from the official Windows release ZIP. I don't launch a separate terminal emulator; this console-style window is what appears.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm launching hx inside a terminal with bracketed paste enabled, and ordinary clipboard paste works normally everywhere in Helix.

edges.comment: Opening report and reporter comments c1-c4/c8: n8henrie explains that hx.exe is double-clicked directly and supplies a screenshot of the resulting window. The additional clipboard and health facts were volunteered by the same reporter in c2-c3.

solution.intent: Enable the Windows console Ctrl-Shift-C/V option so the console can paste clipboard text into Helix.
solution.concrete_example: Right-click the console title bar, open Properties, enable the Ctrl-Shift-C/V shortcut option, then use Ctrl-Shift-V to paste.

edges.comment: CptPotato c7 suggested enabling the console shortcut setting. Reporter c8 confirms that this persistently enabled Ctrl-Shift-V and fixed generic insert-mode paste, but the original UNC `:o` operation still advanced at about 13 seconds per character, so it is a blind path for the reported file-opening problem. The helper's settings screenshot is not reused as reporter evidence.

question_patterns: Which exact part of the network path makes the slowdown start?
Does changing the quotes or the leading characters alter the delay?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The quotes make no difference. Both quoted and unquoted paths take about 13 seconds per character when they start with `\\`. If I remove the leading `\\` and leave the remaining backslashes in place, the string pastes with minimal lag.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every long path is equally slow, including local `C:\...` paths and strings without a UNC prefix.
The delay is around ten seconds rather than thirteen seconds per character, but it still begins only with the UNC prefix.

question_patterns: Can you compare the UNC string with an otherwise similar string that still contains backslashes but lacks the leading UNC prefix?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. `1.2.3.4\UsersFiles\me\Desktop\foo.txt` pastes quickly, while `\\1.2.3.4\UsersFiles\me\Desktop\foo.txt` is extremely slow.

question_patterns: Does the same complete UNC string paste slowly in the editor pane too, or only in the command prompt?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The complete quoted UNC path pastes into the editor pane without trouble. Using the same Ctrl-Shift-V paste in the command pane after `:o ` makes the characters trickle in one at a time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The UNC path is equally slow in the editor pane, the command prompt, and other console applications.

question_patterns: Can you share the Helix log produced while opening or dragging the network file?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log repeats `failed to open git repo`, `NoGitRepository`, `failed to open diff base`, and `failed to obtain current head name` for the `\\?\UNC\1.2.3.4\UsersFiles\me\Desktop` path.

edges.comment: Reporter c4, c9, c16 and c19: n8henrie supplies raw logs and controlled comparisons showing that backslashes themselves work and that the delay is specific to a leading UNC path in the `:o` command prompt.

solution.intent: Attribute the behavior entirely to the lack of bracketed paste in the default Windows console and advise starting Helix in a terminal emulator that supports bracketed paste.
solution.concrete_example: Start Helix from a bracketed-paste-capable terminal emulator instead of double-clicking the TUI executable; the terminal is otherwise feeding each pasted character as keyboard input.

edges.comment: Maintainer response c17 attributed the issue to cmd.exe lacking bracketed paste. The same reporter challenged this with the editor-versus-command comparison in c18-c19 and later reported in c20 that Helix 23.10 reproduces in Windows Terminal 1.18, which supports bracketed paste. The reporter also observed instant insertion after invalid `:e ` but a stall after valid `:o ` at a directory with many children, falsifying the brush-off as a complete explanation.

solution.intent: Open the copied network path through Helix's system-clipboard register expansion in the `:open` prompt instead of pasting or dragging the UNC path character by character.
solution.concrete_example: Use Shift-right-click and `Copy as path` in Explorer, then enter `:o <C-r>*` in Helix and press Enter. Helix inserts the clipboard path, which may appear as `\\?\UNC\...`, and opens the network file efficiently.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence distinguishes generic terminal clipboard transport from Helix's handling of incrementally entered paths in the valid `:o` prompt: the same UNC text is immediate in the editor and after invalid `:e`, reproduces in bracketed-paste-capable Windows Terminal, and becomes slow near a network directory with many children. The thread does not establish a lower-level implementation defect, so the diagnosis should not invent one.

edges.comment: Reporter c21 supplies and confirms the final practical resolution on their own Windows network share: `:o <C-r>*` opens the system clipboard buffer directly and works much more efficiently. No code-level fix or deeper implementation mechanism was established in the thread.

satisfaction_conditions: Must recognize that the extreme delay is specific to entering a UNC path in Helix's valid `:o` prompt, especially as it reaches a network directory with many subdirectories; it is not a general inability to paste backslashes.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the reporter's comparisons: the same UNC text pastes immediately into the editor, a non-UNC-prefixed backslash path is fast, invalid `:e` receives the path immediately, and the issue reproduces in bracketed-paste-capable Windows Terminal.
Must not treat enabling Ctrl-Shift-V or switching to a bracketed-paste-capable terminal as the complete fix; both directions were tested and the UNC `:o` slowdown remained.
The practical resolution must use Helix's system clipboard register in the open prompt, `:o <C-r>*`, rather than feeding the UNC path character by character.
Must ask the user to verify that the copied network file opens efficiently and only treat the issue as resolved after that confirmation.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Unix, SSH, nvim, and TUI user who is unfamiliar with Windows console behavior and Helix-specific clipboard/register commands; unable to install build dependencies due to restricted administrator access.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, persistent, and evidence-driven. Provides exact keystrokes, timings, logs, controlled string comparisons, and follow-up tests; challenges explanations carefully when observations do not fit.
